hate.d: the emotion of intense dislike; a feeling of dislike so strong that it demands action

hatched.d: shaded by means of fine parallel or crossed lines

hatred.d: the emotion of intense dislike; a feeling of dislike so strong that it demands action

hat.d: headdress that protects the head from bad weather; has shaped crown and usually a brim

hatchet.d: weapon consisting of a fighting ax; used by North American Indians

hatchback.d: a sloping rear car door that is lifted to open

hatching.d: shading consisting of multiple crossing lines

hatchery.d: a place where eggs are hatched under artificial conditions (especially fish eggs)

hatter.d: someone who makes and sells hats

hatted.d: wearing a hat or a hat of a particular kind

hatchway.d: an entrance equipped with a hatch; especially a passageway between decks of a ship

hatbox.d: a round piece of luggage for carrying hats

hatemonger.d: one who arouses hatred for others

hatiora.d: small genus of South American epiphytic or lithophytic cacti

hatband.d: a band around the crown of a hat just above the brim

hatrack.d: a rack with hooks for temporarily holding coats and hats

hatpin.d: a long sturdy pin used by women to secure a hat to their hair

hatmaker.d: someone who makes and sells hats

hatful.d: (often followed by `of') a large number or amount or extent

hate mail.d: mail that expresses the writer's dislike or hatred (usually in offensive language)

hatchet job.d: a false accusation of an offense or a malicious misrepresentation of someone's words or actions

hat trick.d: (sports) three consecutive scores by one player or three scores in one game (as in cricket or ice hockey etc.)

hatchet man.d: one whose job it is to execute unpleasant tasks for a superior
